title: Chapter 229: The Flyer for Ghost Stories Society
html:
“No matter where I was, whenever the sun rose and I awoke from my dreams, I told myself it was a new day. Yet each time I opened my eyes, the monster within me awakened too. It tore my wounds open again and again, and the pain pierced to the bone, reminding me.

“I’m my children’s killer, the source of all tragedy.

“I sought help from doctors. They said the monster was my conscience and guilt given form—that I was torturing myself.

“They suggested I focus on something else and find a place where my heart could rest.

“I was afraid of other people, so I sought refuge in medicine, books, and religion.

“I carried one small hope in my heart: perhaps God could forgive my sins and grant me salvation.

“In everyone else’s eyes, I was my children’s murderer, but God would not see me that way. I would give Him everything.

“Three years ago, the pain finally stopped. Perhaps the medicine was working. I truly felt myself improving, becoming more at peace.

“In the autumn of the fourth year, the police brought a stranger to me. They said he was one of the men who had harmed my wife. He had come seeking forgiveness. But why should I forgive him?

“My wife lost all three of her children, and not long afterward, she was taken from me forever. I will never forgive him. Never!

“The stranger bared his heart to me, but I felt not a shred of pity. If anything, I thought he had not suffered enough. People like him do not deserve forgiveness.

“When he finished, he seemed relieved. His relief enraged me. I lunged at him, and during the struggle, the chain around his neck snapped. A locket engraved with the image of God fell to the floor.

“Terrified that his greatest treasure would be trampled, he shielded the locket with his body and begged God for forgiveness.

“I saw myself in that man. We were alike, down to the God inside our lockets. I owned the very same locket—we worshipped the same God!

“Why would my God forgive the murderer who harmed my wife?

“After the stranger left, I smashed the locket around my neck and burned every religious object in my home.

“The monster that had lain silent for four years awoke once more. I thought I had healed, but I had only lied to myself. Yet this was perfect. I no longer needed to suppress the monster that had become part of me.

“I found a knife in the kitchen and went after the stranger.

“God might have forgiven him, but I had not.”

Bloody writing filled the wall. Much more followed, but the sentences became increasingly incoherent, though all retained the tone of a confession.

The longer Guo Miao stared, the more frightened he became. “Could this be Boss Chen’s past? Was he once the patient in this room? Did he wear this face as a mask?”

His imagination ran wild, feeding his fear. “Could this be real human skin?”

Gritting his teeth, he held his breath and reached toward the face. Just before his fingertip touched it, a scream erupted in the corridor.

“Who was that? I saw it! A face! There was a face inside Room 3!” The woman’s shrill scream turned Guo Miao’s legs to water, and he collapsed. Heart pounding, he pressed a hand to his chest and turned to shout through the doorway—then something caught his eye. From where he knelt before the embedded face, he could see a yellowed piece of paper protruding from the gap between it and the wall.

“What is this?” Hands trembling, he reached behind the face and began working the paper free. Taking care not to damage the face, Guo Miao finally extracted a sheet about the size of his palm.

“Ghost Stories Society?” It appeared to be a flyer. An image of a half-open red door covered the back, while the upper half of the front bore the words ‘Ghost Stories Society.’ The lower half explained how to enter the society.

“Look for a building with twenty-four floors and take the elevator at midnight?”

Clutching the paper, Guo Miao felt his heart skip beat after beat. He could no longer distinguish reality from illusion. At the same moment he discovered the flyer, Chen Ge emerged from the hidden passage into Room 3, and the black phone in his pocket vibrated.

A message now?Chen Ge withdrew into the passage, closed the steel door, and checked the phone.

“You’ve triggered the only hidden mission inside Third Sick Hall—Ghost Stories Society!

“This will be your first opponent before you master nightmares! Find them!

“Mission Hint One: The Ghost Stories Society meets in one of the rooms on the twenty-fourth floor.

“Mission Hint Two: A building has twenty-three floors, but its elevator has twenty-four numbered buttons. Why?

“Mission Hint Three: Only by taking the elevator at midnight can you enter the twenty-fourth floor.”

While waiting for the elevator at Fang Hwa Apartments, Chen Ge had discovered by chance that the building possessed only twenty-three floors, yet its elevator had twenty-four numbered buttons.

The Ghost Stories Society is inside that building?

Inside Room 10, Guo Miao held his phone close to the flyer. “Only by taking the elevator at midnight can you find the Ghost Stories Society. Enter the elevator and travel to the twenty-third floor. From there, descend to the second floor. Once you reach the second floor, ascend to the twenty-second. Repeat this pattern several times, then press the button for the twenty-fourth floor.”

The instructions alone frightened Guo Miao. He refolded the flyer and pushed it back beneath the human face.

“This must be some kind of prank, right? Riding an elevator alone at midnight, traveling endlessly up and down... Every time the doors open onto a corridor, what if one of those things gets in with you?

“This place is too strange. We can’t stay any longer. Old Song, help me up—we’re leaving!”

Chen Ge pocketed his black phone and swung the hammer before him. The visitors have triggered the hidden mission. How did they manage to do that?

Before opening the Third Sick Hall to visitors, Chen Ge had inspected every corner of the scenario, including Room 10. The flyer, however, was expertly concealed. It could be seen only by looking up at the face from floor level. In other words, someone had to be so frightened by the face that they fell down before they could discover it. Guo Miao had found it by pure coincidence.

When Chen Ge had first seen the face, by contrast, he had walked over and squeezed its nose and cheeks to test it. He had not been afraid in the slightest. If anything, he had been pleased, suspecting that it belonged to Patient 10 and brought him one step closer to solving the mystery.

The visitors discovered the hidden mission. I should thank them properly.

Hearing footsteps outside the passage, he touched the skin mask covering his face and waited for the perfect moment.
